episode.title: Fail closed when restricted shell-command arguments cannot be parsed in automatic-approval mode
episode.before: At parent cfd7541ad45b25109744c988ac5fc8128accb0ec, shell-command policy evaluation treated only an empty parsed-command list as a parsing failure. When that occurred in YOLO automatic-approval mode, it returned ALLOW even if the matched rule contained an argsPattern restriction. A parser result containing command details plus hasError=true was not treated as failure and continued through normal subcommand validation.
episode.after: At ed469e492b4190ce8983b9dd1c5fb5b9f1b140d0, an empty parsed-command list or parser-reported error enters the failure path. Existing explicit DENY decisions remain DENY. In YOLO mode, a matched rule with an argsPattern now returns DENY because its argument restriction cannot be reliably validated; an unrestricted rule may still return ALLOW. Outside YOLO mode, parsing failures continue to use the configured default decision.
episode.diff: The implementation broadened the shell parse-failure predicate from subCommands.length === 0 to subCommands.length === 0 || parsed?.hasError, then inserted a YOLO-mode guard that forces DENY when the matched rule has an argsPattern. Two unit tests mock the parser to return respectively no details with an error and nonempty details with an error, and verify that a restricted ALLOW rule cannot authorize the shell command in either case.

evidence_units.claim: Commit ed469e492b4190ce8983b9dd1c5fb5b9f1b140d0 has parent cfd7541ad45b25109744c988ac5fc8128accb0ec, is titled "fix(core): fail closed in YOLO mode when shell parsing fails for restricted rules (#25935)", and changes the policy engine and its unit test.
The parent implementation considered parsing failed only when no subcommands were returned and, in YOLO mode, returned ALLOW without checking whether the matched rule constrained arguments.
The change expands the invalid-parse condition to cover both an empty details list and parsed.hasError, including cases where partial command details exist.
evidence_units.source: git diff cfd7541ad45b25109744c988ac5fc8128accb0ec ed469e492b4190ce8983b9dd1c5fb5b9f1b140d0 -- packages/core/src/policy/policy-engine.ts; resulting file lines 363-368

evidence_units.claim: On an invalid parse, the new YOLO branch returns DENY when the matched rule has argsPattern; without an argument restriction it preserves YOLO's ALLOW behavior. Explicit DENY and non-YOLO default-decision behavior remain intact.

PolicyEngine.check identifies registered shell tools, matches policy rules against the tool call and serialized arguments, and routes matched shell calls with the matched rule into checkShellCommand, so the guard controls the decision returned for actual restricted shell-tool checks.
A unit test mocks parsing of "echo bypass" as details=[] and hasError=true, configures an argsPattern-restricted ALLOW rule in YOLO mode, and expects the policy decision to be DENY.
A second unit test returns a nonempty command detail together with hasError=true and verifies that the same restricted YOLO-mode ALLOW rule still yields DENY.
The complete change consists of 12 implementation-line changes and 76 test-line changes across two files, with 85 insertions and 3 deletions.

candidate_atomics.name: Deny restricted automatic shell authorization when parsing is invalid
candidate_atomics.description: Treat absent or error-bearing parse results as incapable of proving that a shell command satisfies argument restrictions, and fail closed instead of inheriting automatic approval.

semantic_action.intent: Prevent automatic execution from bypassing argument-scoped shell policy when command parsing cannot reliably validate the arguments.
semantic_action.pre_state: A shell tool call has matched a policy rule, automatic approval is active, the rule constrains arguments, and parsing returns no usable commands or reports an error.
semantic_action.post_state: The authorization result is DENY; parse uncertainty cannot turn an argument-restricted rule into permission to execute.
semantic_action.validation: Unit tests inject both complete parse failure and partial parse output marked erroneous, then assert DENY for a restricted rule in automatic-approval mode.

candidate_workflows.name: Close an automatic-approval bypass caused by uncertain command parsing
candidate_workflows.description: At the shell authorization boundary, classify parser-reported errors as invalid validation results and deny execution when an argument-scoped rule cannot be verified, while preserving explicit denials and the established behavior for unrestricted or non-automatic cases.
atomic_names: Deny restricted automatic shell authorization when parsing is invalid

workflow_graph.goal: Ensure automatic approval cannot authorize a shell command through an argument-restricted rule when parsing is absent, partial, or erroneous.
workflow_graph.entry_state: A shell command reaches policy evaluation under automatic approval and matches a rule whose permission depends on an argument pattern, but the parser cannot provide an error-free decomposition.
workflow_graph.exit_state: The command is denied before execution, and tests cover both empty-error and partial-error parser results.
